limits: Verified never means interoperability with a device the design talks to unless a board measurement against that device is listed in the record; a design that checks its own output against its own model accepts its own symmetric mistakes.

Verified never means timing beyond the stated corner: a post-route timing result is for the part, speed grade, clock and tool version in its evidence file, not for other corners, temperatures or devices.

Verified never means beyond the widths and depths checked: a simulation covers the vectors it ran, a bounded formal result covers the stated depth only, and a per-width proof covers the widths it names; only a Lean proof marked all widths covers every width, and only for its model.

Verified never means the requirement is the right one: the text of a requirement is the human's check (or the planner's, where the record says delegated), and a record shows that checks exist and pass, not that nothing was left out.
Verified never means a hardware or board result unless a board measurement item is listed; a simulation is not the board.
Verified is about the files in the manifest at the hashes given. A change to any of them makes the record out of date (the CI check fails), and the evidence stale until it is re-recorded.
An agreement or acceptance recorded as delegated is the planner's decision on the owner's delegation, not a human sign-off; the record counts it apart.
name: fp_mul
notes: Arithmetic library, function fp_mul (brief 139e). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

item_views.title: Rounding increment carries into the exponent

requirements.source: arith/fp_common/fp_pack.sv (wsum: the increment added to the packed pattern)
requirements.text: For a packed pattern e * m + f with fraction f < m (m = 2^MAN), adding the rounding increment 1 either raises the fraction by one or, when the fraction is all ones, raises the exponent by one and leaves a zero fraction: the identity fp_pack's single add on the packed {exponent, fraction} pattern rests on, so a significand overflow, a subnormal rounding up to the smallest normal number and a largest finite number rounding up to infinity need no special case. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Rounding increment carries into the exponent, for every width

item_views.title: Normalising left by NW - 1 - msb puts the leading one at the top

requirements.source: arith/fp_common/fp_norm.sv (the shift by the leading-zero count)
requirements.text: For a value v with its leading one at bit k (2^k <= v < 2^(k+1)) and k < NW, shifting left by NW - 1 - k places gives a value in [2^(NW-1), 2^NW): the leading one is at bit NW - 1, which is what fp_norm's count lz = NW - 1 - msb does. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Normalising left by NW - 1 - msb puts the leading one at the top, for every width

item_views.title: The rounding decision is round-to-nearest, ties to even

requirements.text: For a kept part hi and a discarded part lo below the threshold 2h, incrementing hi exactly when lo > h, or lo = h and hi is odd (the guard-and-sticky rule of fp_pack), gives a value within h of the exact one and, when it is exactly h away, even. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
